title: Dependency-Aware Invalidation of Inherited Empirical Claims via Code, Model, and Runtime Hashes
target_platform: Local deterministic dependency graph evaluator; audit_decay.py; disclose.py; relay.py; evaluating-agent-work usage telemetry
hypothesis: Binding reusable conclusions to explicit dependencies (relevant code/configuration hashes, model identity, runtime version, and evaluation conditions) will detect >= 95% of materially stale claims with <= 10% unnecessary invalidations while executing <= 30% of a full benchmark rerun measured cost across a fixed mutation suite.
falsification_criteria: More than 5% of materially stale claims remain eligible for unqualified reuse; unnecessary invalidations exceed 10%; selected revalidation costs exceed 30% of full reruns; or any declared safety-critical dependency change leaves its dependent claim marked currently verified. If dependency maintenance exceeds rerun savings, abandon broad deployment and retain only high-value bindings.
experiment: Use 12 previously measured claims and 60 controlled repository/environment mutations (implementation changes, model changes, altered config, unrelated edits, documentation edits). Compare: (1) existing age-based decay, (2) invalidate everything after any repo change, (3) dependency-specific invalidation. Run full evaluations to establish ground truth; measure tests chosen by the selective policy. Preserve prior findings as historical evidence while qualifying present applicability.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Escalate to targeted model evaluations only for models specifically referenced in invalidated claims.
